title: PrivGate: Steering Contextual Integrity in LLMs via Latent Space Geometry
src: https://icml.cc/virtual/2026/poster/61631 (abstract only; no arXiv found, OpenReview PDF excluded)
evidence: Full text not accessible; coded from ICML abstract only. 'Latent Gating ... triggers explicit reasoning only when high latent risk is detected' (linear probe on residual stream gates CI reasoning by the agent model). '62.6% average relative reduction in privacy leakage with 15.9% token overhead'. Threat model/adaptive/n_models/utility/FPR unverifiable.

title: Improving Alignment and Robustness with Circuit Breakers
bench: HarmBench; own:harmful function-calling requests (100); own:multimodal harmful image-text set
evidence: Attacks run against RR (circuit-breaker) models incl. GCG/PAIR/TAP-T/AutoDAN and 'three powerful attacks that leverage system-level and representation-space access' (prefilling, input-embedding attack that 'optimizes the soft input embeddings', RepE attack). Models: Mistral-7B-Instruct-v2, Llama-3-8B-Instruct, LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B (agent set: Llama-3-8B only). Utility MT-Bench/OpenLLM/BFCL; FPR = WildChat refusal 3.4%/6.2%. Overhead only qualitative ('without additional computational burden'); judge sees user prompts only.

title: When Actions Go Off-Task: Detecting and Correcting Misaligned Actions in Computer-Use Agents
evidence: No adaptive/guard-targeted attack; only error analysis: 'well-disguised malicious instructions can deceive the fast check and injection analysis'. DeAction = prompted off-the-shelf LLM guard intercepting each proposed action pre-execution; sees screenshot ('Injection Analysis inspects the current screenshot'); flagged action gets structured feedback and agent re-proposes. Agents: Claude Sonnet 4.5, OpenAI CUA, OpenCUA-72B. FPR via offline precision (88.2%); 11.3 s/step. v1 date from alphaxiv v1 page (arXiv abs history not rendered).

title: CausalArmor: Efficient Indirect Prompt Injection Guardrails via Causal Attribution
evidence: No CausalArmor-specific adaptive attack; DoomArena attacker 'adaptively generates IPIs by observing the conversation history' (generic, not defense-aware); split-context/distributed attacks only listed as limitation (App. A). At privileged action: proxy LLM (Gemma-3-12B) LOO attribution vs margin tau over untrusted spans; flagged spans rewritten by sanitizer LLM + retroactive CoT masking, then re-query. Agents: Gemini-2.5-flash/Pro, Claude-4.0-Sonnet. Benign latency reported; no FPR.

title: The Oversight Game: Learning to Cooperatively Balance an AI Agent's Safety and Autonomy
evidence: Non-adversarial: 'Rather than assuming an adversarial agent that must be monitored externally, we model the interaction as a cooperative game.' Agent learns PLAY/ASK, human TRUST/OVERSEE (human simulated by separate LoRA policy on Qwen3-30B-A3B); oversee may substitute action or shut down. Safe states: ask 3.9%, oversee 2.7%; risky: ask 99.4%. Policy prompt contents (App. B) not visible, so exposure '?'.

title: EMBGuard: Constructing Hazard-Aware Guardrails for Safe Planning in Embodied Agents
evidence: Non-adversarial physical hazards; no attack evaluation. Fine-tuned Qwen-3-VL 2B/4B guard judges (visual observation, candidate action) and outputs risk label/category/explanation; mitigation left to policy model (GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen-3-VL-32B) — guard flags, does not itself rewrite. Utility = mitigation-action alignment only (no task success). Benign-scenario false positives reported; 0.535/0.719 s per sample. v1 date from alphaxiv v1 page.

title: AIR: Improving Agent Safety through Incident Response
evidence: Unintentional incidents, no attacker/threat model. Post-step incident detection by the agent LLM evaluating NL checks of developer-authored AIR rules (DSL) over env state/observations; containment+recovery then task termination; LLM-synthesized guardrail rules block matching actions 'before any tool invocation'. GPT-5 only. 0 FP on 50+35 safe tasks; safe-task time 1.40-1.44x.

title: Think Twice Before You Act: Enhancing Agent Behavioral Safety with Thought Correction
evidence: No attack targeting Thought-Aligner; fixed benchmarks incl. prompt injection (AgentDojo, InjecAgent) though framing is mainly unintended harm. Fine-tuned Qwen2.5 1.5B/7B corrector gets instruction + history incl. observations and rewrites the current thought before tool action. 6 backbones (GPT-4.1, o3, Claude-Sonnet-4, Qwen3-235B, DeepSeek-V3, Llama-3.3-70B). FPR proxy: thought-level classification precision 95.1/96.3%. <100 ms (1.5B), ~0.11 s (7B).

title: AgentSentinel: An End-to-End and Real-Time Security Defense Framework for Computer-Use Agents
evidence: 'We analyze the performance of AgentSentinel against five potential adaptive attacks ... Each adaptive attack targets a core component of AgentSentinel' (kill monitor, toxic task context, toxic system traces, query-cache poisoning); defends 17/20. Tracer halts sensitive OS operations; rule auditor (configurable policies) then LLM auditor (same LLM as agent, separate instance) over summarized task context incl. tool outputs + traces. Agents: Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet, GPT-4-Turbo, GPT-4o. FPR 10.8%, task failure 4.2%, 2.8 security queries per tool use; no latency numbers.

title: SAGA: A Security Architecture for Governing AI Agentic Systems
bench: own:SAGA agent tasks (calendar scheduling, expense-report email, collaborative writing)
evidence: Protocol-aware attacks A1-A8 (rogue/compromised agents, forged credentials, missing/expired tokens, policy violation, token sharing) designed against SAGA: 'We implemented these attacker models in our evaluation.' No LLM in enforcement: Provider checks user-written contact policies; encrypted access-control tokens with expiry/quota checked per request. Content-level injection out of scope. LLMs: GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1, Qwen-2.5-72B. Crypto ~1-2 ms; protocol <0.6% of end-to-end.

title: Firewalls to Secure Dynamic LLM Agentic Networks
evidence: Limitations: 'We do not evaluate adaptive attacks where an adversary is aware of the firewall design and actively optimizes attacks against it.' Language Converter LLM reads external-agent messages and maps them to a closed structured protocol, then deterministic validation; Data Abstraction firewall abstracts user data before it reaches the assistant. Protocol/rules generated offline by an LLM from demonstration corpora. Assistants: GPT-5, Claude Sonnet 4, Gemini 2.5 Pro/Flash. ConVerse = Gomaa et al. 2026 (same group). No overhead/FPR.

title: VeriSafe Agent: Safeguarding Mobile GUI Agent via Logic-based Action Verification
evidence: Safety against erroneous GUI-agent actions, no attacker. GPT-4o autoformalizes the user instruction (with developer-library predicates) into DSL rules once per task; deterministic Intent Verifier checks each action using states returned by the in-app developer library; failing actions discarded with rule-based feedback. FPR 2.7%, FNR 0.7%. Only M3A + GPT-4o.

title: Prompt-to-SQL Injections in LLM-Integrated Web Applications: Risks and Defenses
evidence: Defenses only tested against the fixed attack set (U.1-U.3, RD, RI); bypass acknowledged but untested: 'potential circumvention through targeted attacks that can bypass the LLM guard's prompt template instructions'. Defenses: DB permission hardening, SQL query rewriting (pre-exec), LLM guard checking SQL results before LLM context, in-prompt data preloading. Defense eval with gpt-3.5-turbo-0301 only. LLM guard ~0.4 s; rewriting 1.87 ms. v1 date from alphaxiv v1 page.
